questions.answer:

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain the store of value function of money with an example.
questions.answer: Money keeps purchasing power for later use. Sushila cannot store mangoes for long, but she can keep the ₹250 she got by selling them and spend it later.

questions.q: Explain money as a measure of value.
questions.answer: Money is the common unit in which the value of every good is expressed. Value = price × quantity: 25 kg of rice at ₹20 a kg is worth ₹500. This makes it easy to compare goods.

or.q: Explain the lack of divisibility under barter.
or.answer: Some goods cannot be divided into small parts. A person with a cow cannot cut it up to exchange part of it for cloth and part for grain, so small exchanges become impossible.

questions.q: What is the barter system? Give an example.
questions.answer: Barter is the exchange of goods and services for other goods and services without money. Examples: 10 kg of wheat for 5 kg of sugar, or 8 kg of rice for a pair of shoes.

questions.q: Explain money as a medium of exchange.
questions.answer: People buy and sell goods and services using money. The seller receives money and the buyer pays it: you pay ₹10 and get a pen. This removes the need for double coincidence of wants.

questions.q: Why was it difficult to equate the values of different goods under barter?
questions.answer: There was no common unit of measurement. A cow cannot be divided, and no one good could measure the value of all others, so it was hard to say how much cloth or grain equalled a cow.

questions.q: What is double coincidence of wants?
questions.answer: For a barter exchange, each person must want what the other has. A person with rice who wants cloth must find someone who has cloth and wants rice. Without this, no exchange can take place.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain money as a standard of deferred payment with an example.
questions.answer:
Money is used to make payments in the future. A friend borrows ₹300 to buy a book and promises to repay it after a week with ₹1 interest, i.e. ₹301.
The lender accepts money because it keeps its value; a used book would not be accepted.
So loans and future payments are settled in money.

questions.q: What is money? State two of its functions.
questions.answer:
Money is anything generally accepted as a medium of exchange, which also serves as a unit of account, a store of value and a means of repaying debt.
(1) Medium of exchange: goods are bought and sold for money.
(2) Measure of value: prices and values of goods are expressed in money.

questions.q: 'The lack of double coincidence of wants is a common problem with the barter system.' Explain.
questions.answer:
In barter, the person with rice who wants cloth must find someone who has cloth and wants rice.
Such a match is rare, so exchange often does not take place and much time is wasted searching, especially when transport and communication were poor.
Money solves this, since anyone accepts money for their goods.

questions.q: Explain the main demerits of the barter system.
questions.answer:
(1) Lack of double coincidence of wants.
(2) Lack of divisibility — a cow cannot be split.
(3) No common measure of value.
(4) Large stocks had to be stored for trade.
(5) Perishable goods could not store value, so lending and future payment were not possible.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the functions of money: medium of exchange and measure of value.
questions.answer:
Medium of exchange: the primary function. People sell goods for money and use money to buy other goods; you pay ₹10 for a pen and the seller receives ₹10. Exchange no longer needs a double coincidence of wants, and buying and selling become quick and easy.
Measure of value: money is the common unit of account. The value of every good is expressed in money, value = price × quantity — a 25 kg bag of rice at ₹20 a kg is worth ₹500. This makes comparison, accounting and pricing simple, which was not possible under barter.

questions.q: Why did the need for money arise? Explain the demerits of barter.
questions.answer:
Money arose because barter failed.
(1) Lack of double coincidence of wants — a matching trader was hard to find.
(2) Lack of divisibility — a cow cannot be divided to buy small items.
(3) No common measure of value — values of different goods could not be equated.
(4) Storage — large stocks of goods had to be kept in warehouses.
(5) No store of value — perishable goods lost value, so lending and future payment were impossible.
People therefore adopted money, a common medium that is easy to carry and store and that expresses value.

questions.q: Define money and explain its four functions.
questions.answer:
Money is anything generally accepted by society as a medium of exchange, which also acts as a unit of account, a store of value and a means of repaying debt.
(1) Medium of exchange — goods are bought and sold for money.
(2) Measure of value — value is expressed in money (price × quantity).
(3) Store of value — money holds purchasing power for later use.
(4) Standard of deferred payment — loans are repaid in money at a future date, with interest.
